raw_content:
{
  "hook": "This 100% Syrah Gigondas comes from vineyards on the rocky slopes of the Dentelles de Montmirail, where limestone scree and stony marl force deep roots and concentrate savory flavors. Certified biodynamic and vegan, des Bosquets ages the 2023 for 18 months in oak, producing a peppery, mineral-driven Syrah that reads more Northern Rhône than typical Grenache-led Gigondas.",
  "wine_summary": "Des Bosquets' Les Routes matters because it flips the Gigondas script: rather than rely on Grenache's plush fruit it pushes Syrah's pepper, olive and dark-plum profile into the foreground. The producer's biodynamic and organic practices reduce yields and preserve skin health, intensifying phenolic ripeness and savory aromatics. Critical response supports the approach — multiple mid-90 scores (including 94–95 points across recent releases) — indicating this is being taken seriously by reviewers who value varietal precision and textural density.",
  "terroir_expression": "Thin, rocky soils on the Dentelles — limestone bedrock, decomposed limestone scree and patches of stony marl — retain daytime heat while the limestone imparts mineral lift; that combination concentrates dark fruit and gives Syrah a saline, stone-driven bite. The jagged peaks create diurnal cooling at night, preserving black-pepper rotundone and keeping tannins firm rather than jammy.",
  "vinification_summary": "The 2023 spent 18 months in oak, a choice that softens tannin through slow micro-oxygenation and layers in toast and spice; des Bosquets' biodynamic farming likely yields grapes with thicker skins and greater phenolic concentration, but specific cooperage and fermentation regimes are not publicly detailed. Limited public data on whole-cluster use or maceration length means we must infer that structure comes from ripe skins plus extended élevage rather than high new-oak extraction.",
  "food_pairing": "Start casual: Nashville hot chicken — the wine's pepper and acidity cut the fried fat while dark fruit cools the heat. Fine dining: roasted lamb shoulder with herbes de Provence and black olive tapenade — tannin and olive notes mirror the dish and lift the savory sauce. Rustic classic: cassoulet (duck confit and white beans) — the wine's structure stands up to long-cooked meat and the limestone-driven acidity keeps the dish from feeling heavy. Barbecue: smoked beef short ribs with a pepper-forward rub — the wine echoes the smoke and complements the beefy umami.",
  "comparable_wines": "Domaine Santa Duc Gigondas 'Les Hautes Garrigues' — comparable for its density, peppery Syrah contribution and similar price/quality slot in Gigondas. Domaine du Cayron Gigondas — similar for focused, minerally fruit and a more savory, structured take on the village.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry Syrah with firm tannins and peppery, mineral savoryity",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink from 2026 through 2036 for the best balance of primary fruit and developed tertiary notes; store at cellar temperature (12–14°C) on its side with steady humidity.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $30–$60 retail. Competitors in this bracket include Domaine Santa Duc Gigondas and Domaine du Cayron Gigondas. This is worth the price for buyers who want a Syrah-forward, terroir-driven Gigondas with mid-90 critic recognition and clear aging potential; it delivers more structure and pepper than similarly priced Grenache-led village wines.",
  "market_position": "Restaurant lists that feature Rhône diversity and retail shops aimed at Rhône-curious collectors will stock this; it's aimed at sommeliers and serious drinkers who want a savory alternative to Grenache-dominant Gigondas. It also fits private cellar rotations for collectors seeking mid-term aging rather than instant crowd-pleasers.",
  "insider_take": "Treat Les Routes as Gigondas written by a Northern Rhône player: buy it if you prefer pepper, olive and mineral tension over Grenache's plushness. Skip it if you want the floral, sun-kissed red-fruit comfort of classic Gigondas blends — the tradeoff here is structure and black-fruit concentration versus Grenache's generosity.",
  "aging_potential_years": 12,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,

  }
}
